extracted.intended_audience: general readers and fans seeking an encyclopedic summary of Amy Poehler's book (readers, researchers, casual browsers)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic entry summarizing a single book (Yes Please) including publication details and critical reception. Focus is on descriptive metadata and reviewers' evaluative comments about the book's humor, prose, and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor and honesty (publisher framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Described by the publisher as "full of humor and honesty and brimming with true stories, fictional anecdotes and life lessons."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the publisher's characterization indicating criteria readers might expect: a mixture of humor, candid personal reflection, real stories, fictional vignettes, and takeaways. Serves as marketing expectation rather than critical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of live comedic persona to the page / sharpness
rubrics_metrics.description: Laura Miller: "Yes Please is unable to make a virtue out of its author’s lack of sharp edges. In person, Poehler can do this, and it’s a remarkable achievement, but on the page she tends to wax bland."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether a performer's in-person comedic strengths (sharpness, edge, immediacy) successfully translate into written form; looks for vividness and bite in prose rather than a flattened, bland rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing craft / ability to write prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Dwight Garner: "Yes Please reminds you of that squeaky fact: Even smart, hilarious people, the ones you wish were your great friends, sometimes can't write."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general criterion about basic prose competence: clarity, sentence-level craft, narrative skill. Suggests that comedic talent does not guarantee writing skill and that reviewers judge the quality of the writing itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of comedic effectiveness (what 'works')
rubrics_metrics.description: Mary McNamara: "Not everything in Yes Please works [...], but many things are funny, and as with most of her comedy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether humor is effective across the book or only in parts; reviewers note unevenness — some passages succeed while others fail — so consistency is a key evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose flow and stylistic cohesion (choppiness/self-conscious eccentricity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mary McNamara characterizes the writing as "choppy and self-consciously eccentric."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include narrative flow, transitions, structural coherence, and whether stylistic quirks feel deliberate and effective or distracting and unpolished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity, vulnerability, and self-awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers note that Poehler is "funny and honest," and that she "is a smart and funny woman who isn't either of those things all the time and doesn't mind admitting it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the memoir's tone for sincerity and candidness: does the author appear genuine, self-reflective, and willing to expose weakness or imperfection in service of humor and insight?

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of jokes and self-referential humor about writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rachel Dry: "So she is funny and honest. Writing a book is hard, and that seems to be the truth. At least she made some good jokes about it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the strength of specific jokes, especially meta-jokes about the difficulty of writing the book; measures whether the comedic moments land and contribute to the reader's enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiobook/spoken-word performance recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The audio version of Yes Please received a Grammy nomination for Best Spoken Word Album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External recognition of the audiobook suggests evaluative criteria for the spoken form: narration performance, delivery, timing, and how well the performer conveys humor and tone in audio format.
